subject: journey/zhenghe-5
prompt:
The attached page is from the same journal. Draw a new, different scene as described below, matching its drawing style, paper and palette, and drawing the traveller with the same face, build and clothing. Do not copy its composition.

An illustrated page from an explorer's journal: one particular moment on the journey, drawn close enough to see faces, hands, tools, clothing and the things being traded, measured or found, rather than a distant landscape. In the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries. A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink with loose hatching; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green, faded blue and a touch of red. The page may carry one or two small separate studies of a detail (an object, a tool, a creature) loosely arranged beside the main scene, as on a real sketchbook page. Edges unfinished, dissolving into bare, slightly foxed cream paper; a single page, no binding visible. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, numbers, dates or signature; any writing that appears in the scene is illegible marks. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given; people, dress and objects true to their place and time, drawn with respect.

The traveller: Admiral Zheng He, about forty-five: a tall, broad-shouldered Hui Muslim court eunuch of the Ming, clean-shaven with a strong round face, in a red Ming official's robe with a square embroidered rank badge on the chest, a black gauze winged official hat and a jade belt; often beside him his interpreter Ma Huan, a slight Muslim scholar in a plain blue robe and black cap, holding a writing brush and a folded notebook.

This picture: A pepper market at Calicut on the Malabar coast, 1418. Under a palm-thatched shed, Malayali merchants in white mundu cloths and Chinese officials in Ming robes clasp hands to seal a bargain; a large balance beam scale weighs black peppercorns heaped in baskets; a Nair officer of the king watches. Ma Huan sits on a mat writing in his notebook. Coconut palms and the masts of junks in the roadstead behind. A small separate study on the page shows a sprig of pepper vine with berries.
